claim: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) can disrupt the protective membrane barrier by formation of leaky pores.
source: Peptides with the right properties, for example Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), can disrupt this protective barrier by formation of leaky pores.
evidence: This is a general statement about AMP function that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: The proline/glycine kink in helical peptides was reported to both increase and decrease antimicrobial activity.
source: In particular, the proline/glycine kink in helical peptides was reported to both increase and decrease antimicrobial activity.
evidence: This statement references contradictory findings in the literature, indicating citation-based support.

claim: A kink in helices affects the formation of membrane pores by stabilizing toroidal pores but disrupting barrel-stave pores.
source: We used computer simulations and fluorescence experiments to show that a kink in helices affects the formation of membrane pores by stabilizing toroidal pores but disrupting barrel-stave pores.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by both computational simulations and experimental data.

claim: The position of the proline/glycine kink in the sequence controls the specific structure of toroidal pore.
source: The position of the proline/glycine kink in the sequence further controls the specific structure of toroidal pore.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on simulation data.

claim: Two helical peptides can form a kink-like connection with similar behavior as one long helical peptide with a kink.
source: Moreover, we demonstrate that two helical peptides can form a kink-like connection with similar behavior as one long helical peptide with a kink.
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated through simulations.

claim: Hundreds of thousands of people die each year after contracting an infection caused by drug-resistant bacteria.
source: Each year, hundreds of thousands of people die after contracting an infection caused by drug-resistant bacteria (WHO, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a WHO report.

claim: New classes of antibiotics have not been approved for decades.
source: Moreover, infections by resistant bacteria are projected to become one of the leading causes of premature death in the upcoming decades. Unfortunately, the current rate of introducing novel antimicrobial drugs is very low and new classes of antibiotics have not been approved for decades (Nelson et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: AMPs comprise both host-defense peptides and peptide toxins with antimicrobial activity.
source: AMPs are naturally occurring peptides that comprise of both (1) host-defense peptides, i.e., components of innate immune system of many organisms (Fosgerau and Hoffmann, 2015; Peters et al., 2010) and (2) peptide toxins with antimicrobial activity (Zasloff, 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Thousands of AMPs have been discovered to date.
source: To this day, thousands of AMPs (Wang et al., 2015) were discovered and many of them exhibit their activity (against bacteria, viruses, fungi, or cancer cells) even at micromolar concentrations (Gaspar et al., 2013; Falco et al., 2009; Hoskin and Ramamoorthy, 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: Many AMPs exhibit their activity at micromolar concentrations.
source: To this day, thousands of AMPs (Wang et al., 2015) were discovered and many of them exhibit their activity (against bacteria, viruses, fungi, or cancer cells) even at micromolar concentrations (Gaspar et al., 2013; Falco et al., 2009; Hoskin and Ramamoorthy, 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: AMPs have not been widely adopted as conventional antibiotics due to their common toxicity, increased tendency for degradation by proteases, high cost, and decreased activity in vivo.
source: AMPs have not been adopted as widely as conventional antibiotics due to their common toxicity, increased tendency for degradation by proteases, high cost, and decreased activity in vivo (Mahlapuu et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Rational design of AMPs is not feasible because we lack understanding of the sequence-to-function relationship.
source: Additionally, the rational design is not feasible, because we lack the understanding of the sequence-to-function relationship (Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: A single residue substitution can have profound effect on peptide activity and mechanism of action.
source: Even a single residue substitution can have profound effect on the peptide activity and its mechanism of action (Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Common characteristics of pore-forming AMPs are amphiphilicity, positive net charge, and length ranging from 10 to 50 amino acids.
source: Common characteristics of pore-forming AMPs are: (1) amphiphilicity (spatial clustering of hydrophobic and hydrophilic residues) (Wimley, 2010), (2) positive net charge, and (3) length ranging from 10 to 50 amino acids (Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: AMPs are typically unstructured in solution and can adopt a secondary structure upon interaction with a membrane.
source: AMPs are typically unstructured in solution and can adopt a secondary structure upon interaction with a membrane.
evidence: This is a general statement about AMP behavior based on established knowledge.

claim: Positive net charge of AMPs is responsible for increased selectivity towards bacterial membranes.
source: The effect of individual peptide residues on lipid specificity remains unclear, however, positive net charge of AMPs was shown to be responsible for increased selectivity towards bacterial membranes (Chen et al., 2005; Dathe and Wieprecht, 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: There are two well-established pore models: barrel-stave and toroidal.
source: There are two well-established pore models: (1) barrel-stave and (2) toroidal.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: In barrel-stave pores, hydrophobic residues of AMPs are in contact with the membrane core, while hydrophilic residues form a polar channel.
source: In both pore structures, hydrophobic residues of AMPs are in contact with the membrane core, while hydrophilic residues form a polar channel.
evidence: This is a description of established pore structures.

claim: Barrel-stave pore is a compact, bundle-like assembly of peptides with only a little effect on the neighboring lipids.
source: Barrel-stave pore is a compact, bundle-like assembly of peptides with only a little effect on the neighboring lipids (Pollard et al., 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: In toroidal pores, peptides are loosely arranged and lipid headgroups are present in the polar channel.
source: In contrast, peptides in toroidal pores are loosely arranged and the lipid headgroups are present in the polar channel (Sengupta et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: The kink and helix-kink-helix motif have been shown to be biologically relevant for the activity of AMPs.
source: The kink (Vanhoof et al., 1995; Lee et al., 2013) and helix-kink-helix motif (Kozic et al., 2018) have been shown to be biologically relevant for the activity of AMPs.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: Methodologically diverse studies have produced contradictory results, reporting the helical kink to both enhance and reduce antimicrobial effects.
source: However, methodologically diverse studies have produced contradictory results, reporting the helical kink to both enhance (Xiao et al., 2009; Suh et al., 1999; Lim et al., 2005; Shin et al., 2001; Suh et al., 1996; Kobayashi et al., 2000; Tieleman et al., 2001; Rodríguez et al., 2014; Corzo et al., 2001; Vermeer et al., 2012; Amos et al., 2016) and reduce (Park et al., 2002; Gehman et al., 2008; Liu et al., 2011) antimicrobial effects.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations showing contradictory findings.

claim: The presence of kink is unfavorable for the formation of barrel-stave pore because the kink-induced increased flexibility hinders the tight packing of peptides inside barrel-stave pores.
source: The presence of kink was found to be unfavorable for the formation of the barrel-stave pore, because the (kink-induced) increased flexibility hinders the tight packing of peptides inside barrel-stave pores.
evidence: This is a finding from the Monte Carlo simulations presented in the study.

claim: Peptides forming toroidal pores benefit from the kink-induced flexibility.
source: In contrast, peptides forming toroidal pores benefit from the kink-induced flexibility as can be seen in Figure 1B, where free energy profiles for half-hydrophobic peptides of length 7 nm are displayed.
evidence: This is a finding from the Monte Carlo simulations shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A pore can be created by association between surface-aligned and transmembrane peptides.
source: A pore can be also created by association between surface-aligned and transmembrane peptides.
evidence: This is a finding from the simulations.

claim: A mixture of suitable AMPs could possess synergistic interactions responsible for more efficient pore formation.
source: It has been suggested that a mixture of suitable AMPs could possess synergistic interactions responsible for more efficient pore formation (Salnikov and Bechinger, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Synergistic pores were observed to be created by half-hydrophobic peptides with the helix-kink-helix motif in simulations.
source: In our simulations, we have observed these synergistic pores created by half-hydrophobic peptides with the helix-kink-helix motif.
evidence: This is a finding from the simulations.

claim: The calculated free energy profiles show the preference for the angle of 135° compared to 90° between peptides in synergistic pores.
source: In agreement with the experimental evidence (Strandberg et al., 2016), the calculated free energy profiles show the preference for the angle of 135° compared to 90°.
evidence: This is a finding from the simulations that agrees with experimental evidence cited.

claim: Flexible kink was observed to be favorable for the formation of toroidal pores for peptides bound on the membrane at sufficiently high concentration.
source: For peptides that were bound on the membrane at sufficiently high concentration, flexible kink was observed to be favorable for the formation of toroidal pores.
evidence: This is a finding from the Monte Carlo simulations.

claim: Flexible peptides with a total length exceeding the membrane thickness can adopt Hourglass or U-shaped structures.
source: Interestingly, flexible peptides with a total length exceeding the membrane thickness can adopt Hourglass (Jung et al., 1994) or U-shaped (Santo and Berkowitz, 2012) structures.
evidence: This is a finding from the simulations with references to previous work describing these structures.

claim: In the Hourglass structure, peptides span the membrane.
source: In the Hourglass structure, peptides span the membrane.
evidence: This is a description of a structure observed in simulations.

claim: In the U-shape structure, both peptide termini are anchored on the same leaflet and the peptide inserts into the membrane only with its central part.
source: In the U-shape structure, both peptide termini are anchored on the same leaflet and the peptide inserts into the membrane only with its central part.
evidence: This is a description of a structure observed in simulations.

claim: Barrel-stave pores are formed by rigid membrane-spanning peptides with high hydrophobic content.
source: Barrel-stave pores are formed by rigid membrane-spanning peptides with high hydrophobic content.
evidence: This is a finding from the phenomenological model simulations.

claim: In the phenomenological model, peptide-peptide interactions are realized solely via hydrophobic interactions.
source: In our phenomenological model, peptide-peptide interactions are realized solely via hydrophobic interactions.
evidence: This is a description of the model used in the study.

claim: Significant portion of the peptide surface had to be hydrophobic (i.e., sector of at least 270°) for barrel-stave pore formation.
source: Thus, significant portion of the peptide surface had to be hydrophobic (i.e., sector of at least 270°).
evidence: This is a finding from the phenomenological model simulations.

claim: Formation of toroidal pores was observed over a broader range of peptide properties compared to barrel-stave pores.
source: Compared to barrel-stave pores, formation of toroidal pores was observed over a broader range of peptide properties.
evidence: This is a finding from the phenomenological model simulations.

claim: Toroidal pores are formed by weakly associated peptides with hydrophobic sector lower than 270°.
source: Toroidal pores are formed by weakly associated peptides with hydrophobic sector lower than 270°.
evidence: This is a finding from the phenomenological model simulations.

claim: Peptides with hydrophobic sector higher than 310° either aggregate in solution or insert into the membrane without pore formation.
source: Peptides with hydrophobic sector higher than 310° either aggregate in solution or insert into the membrane without pore formation.
evidence: This is a finding from the phenomenological model simulations.

claim: Buforin II wild-type was experimentally shown to translocate across lipid membranes without the formation of membrane pores.
source: Buforin II (Park et al., 1998) wild-type (WT) was experimentally shown to translocate across lipid membranes without the formation of membrane pores.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: The proline kink in Buforin II, located roughly in the middle of the sequence, was identified as a translocation-promoting factor.
source: The proline kink, located roughly in the middle of the sequence, was identified as a translocation-promoting factor (Park et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Rapid closing of the pre-formed pores in POPC membrane was observed for Buforin II WT in agreement with reported findings.
source: In agreement with the reported findings (Park et al., 1998), we have observed rapid closing of the pre-formed pores in POPC membrane for Buforin II WT.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations that agrees with cited experimental findings.

claim: Buforin II WT∗ and helical variants P11L and P11A stabilized pore structure for the whole duration of the simulation of 50 µs.
source: In contrast, Buforin II WT∗ (WT sequence with a fully helical structure without a kink) and helical variants P11L and P11A stabilized pore structure for the whole duration of the simulation of 50 µs.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: Flexible Buforin II variant with a glycine kink, P11G, was unable to stabilize membrane pores.
source: Another flexible Buforin II variant with a glycine kink, P11G, was also unable to stabilize membrane pores.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: The pore stability can be improved by decreasing the peptide flexibility.
source: Appendix 1—figure 4 shows that the pore stability can be improved by decreasing the peptide flexibility.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations shown in a figure.

claim: The stability of Buforin II-formed barrel-stave pores was similar for systems with all considered lipid compositions (POPC, POPC:POPG (1:1 mol/mol), and POPC:POPS (1:1 mol/mol)).
source: The stability of Buforin II-formed barrel-stave pores was similar for systems with all considered lipid compositions (POPC, POPC:POPG (1:1 mol/mol), and POPC:POPS (1:1 mol/mol)), see Appendix 1—figure 3 and Appendix 1—table 3.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: The addition of charged lipids reduced the pore diameter and made the peptide packing even more compact.
source: Generally, the addition of charged lipids reduced the pore diameter and made the peptide packing even more compact, see Appendix 1—figure 3.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: The P11L variant formed the most stable pore across all of the considered membranes.
source: The P11L variant formed the most stable pore across all of the considered membranes.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: The presence of negatively charged lipids affects the morphology of barrel-stave pores.
source: The presence of negatively charged lipids affects the morphology of barrel-stave pores.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: The negatively charged lipid headgroups of POPG and POPS lipids were preferentially pulled into the pore lumen by the positively charged peptide side-chains.
source: The negatively charged lipid headgroups of POPG and POPS lipids were preferentially pulled into the pore lumen by the positively charged peptide side-chains.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: POPG lipids were buried deeper in the hydrophobic core compared to POPS despite the same charge.
source: Despite the same charge, POPG lipids were buried deeper in the hydrophobic core compared to POPS.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations based on phosphate density profiles.

claim: LL-37 is a highly charged peptide that is a part of human innate immune system.
source: LL-37 is a highly charged peptide that is a part of human innate immune system (Turner et al., 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: In an ideal α-helical structure, the LL-37 peptide length would be ∼5.5 nm.
source: In an ideal α-helical structure, the peptide length would be ∼5.5 nm.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the peptide sequence and helical structure.

claim: A kink-induced flexibility of the LL-37 peptide is crucial for the formation of toroidal pores in POPC membrane.
source: A kink-induced flexibility of the LL-37 peptide is crucial for the formation of toroidal pores in POPC membrane.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: The flexible variants of LL-37 (i.e., WT and I13G/G14I) were able to stabilize toroidal pores over the whole duration of the simulation runs.
source: The flexible variants (i.e., WT and I13G/G14I) were able to stabilize toroidal pores over the whole duration of the simulation runs.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: The minimum diameter of the LL-37 WT pore was ∼0.5 nm.
source: The minimum diameter of the LL-37 WT pore was ∼0.5 nm.
evidence: This is a measurement from MARTINI simulations.

claim: Fully-helical variants of LL-37 preferred being adsorbed on membrane surface.
source: In contrast, fully-helical variants preferred being adsorbed on membrane surface.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: The pre-formed pore with LL-37 WT∗ (fully helical secondary structure without kink) completely closed within 5 µs.
source: The pre-formed pore with LL-37 WT∗ (fully helical secondary structure without kink) completely closed within 5 µs and the pore with G14L variant formed only transiently.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: The position of the kink in the LL-37 sequence changes the pore morphology from hourglass to U-shaped.
source: The position of the kink in the LL-37 sequence changes the pore morphology from hourglass to U-shaped.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: In the LL-37 WT sequence, the kink-forming glycine residue is at the interface between hydrophobic and hydrophilic sectors.
source: In the LL-37 WT sequence, the the kink-forming glycine residue (Xhindoli et al., 2016) is at the interface between hydrophobic and hydrophilic sectors.
evidence: This is a structural description based on sequence analysis with a citation.

claim: In the hourglass-shaped pore formed by LL-37 WT, the kink tends to bend the peptide by approximately 90° with the hydrophobic surfaces of the two helical segments facing towards each other.
source: In the pore, the kink tends to bend the peptide by approximately 90° with the hydrophobic surfaces of the two helical segments facing towards each other.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: If the glycine residue is in the middle of the hydrophobic sector (I13G/G14I variant), then the peptide can insert into the membrane pore with its central kink, while the termini stay anchored on the same membrane leaflet.
source: If the glycine residue is in the middle of the hydrophobic sector (I13G/G14I variant), then the peptide can insert into the membrane pore with its central kink, while the termini stay anchored on the same membrane leaflet, see Figure 7B.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: Candidalysin is a cytolytic toxin produced by Candida albicans.
source: Candidalysin is a cytolytic toxin produced by Candida albicans (Moyes et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: As part of the maturation process, Candidalysin is enzymatically truncated several times.
source: As part of the maturation process, Candidalysin is enzymatically truncated several times (Moyes et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Re-positioning of the kink-forming glycine residue in Candidalysin changes the morphology of the pore structure.
source: Similar to the simulations of the LL-37 peptide, re-positioning of the kink-forming glycine residue changes the morphology of the pore structure.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: In the CandKR sequence, the kink is at the interface between the hydrophobic and hydrophilic sectors.
source: In the CandKR sequence, the kink is at the interface between the hydrophobic and hydrophilic sectors.
evidence: This is a structural description based on sequence analysis.

claim: Placing the kink-forming residue in the middle of the hydrophilic patch (P14Q/Q15P) results in the formation of a hourglass pore.
source: Placing the kink-forming residue in the middle of the hydrophilic patch (P14Q/Q15P) results in the formation of a hourglass pore, see Figure 8B.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: During an infection, the predominant form of secreted Candidalysin is terminated with the lysine residue.
source: During an infection, the predominant form of secreted Candidalysin is terminated with the lysine residue, here denoted as CandK (Moyes et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: CandK peptide was experimentally shown to insert into membranes and increase their permeability.
source: Experimentally, this peptide was shown to insert into membranes and increase their permeability (Moyes et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: CandK peptide forms only transient toroidal pores in simulations.
source: Our simulations show that the peptide forms only transient toroidal pores, see Appendix 1—Figure 6.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: Magainin 2 is an amphibian AMP forming toroidal pores.
source: Magainin 2 is an amphibian AMP forming toroidal pores (Ludtke et al., 1996; Matsuzaki et al., 1998b; Yang et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: In the initial stage of pore formation, Magainin 2 was suggested to form a large transient pore that shrinks gradually and becomes more stable.
source: In the initial stage of the pore formation, Magainin 2 was suggested to form a large transient pore that shrinks gradually and becomes more stable (Tamba et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: δ-lysin is a hemolytic peptide (without antimicrobial activity) expressed by Staphylococcus aureus.
source: δ-lysin is a hemolytic peptide (without antimicrobial activity) expressed by Staphylococcus aureus (Alouf et al., 1989; Dhople and Nagaraj, 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: Introduction of proline residue in δ-lysin sequence reduced the hemolytic activity.
source: Introduction of proline residue in the sequence reduced the hemolytic activity and the replacement of all aspartic acid residues to lysine was shown to induce antimicrobial activity (Dhople and Nagaraj, 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Replacement of all aspartic acid residues to lysine in δ-lysin was shown to induce antimicrobial activity.
source: Introduction of proline residue in the sequence reduced the hemolytic activity and the replacement of all aspartic acid residues to lysine was shown to induce antimicrobial activity (Dhople and Nagaraj, 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Both Magainin 2 WT∗ and δ-lysin peptides were observed to form synergistic pores in simulations.
source: Both Magainin 2 WT∗ and δ-lysin peptides were observed to form synergistic pores in our simulations.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: In agreement with experimental findings, Magainin 2 with a glycine kink formed a toroidal pore.
source: In agreement with experimental findings, Magainin 2 with a glycine kink formed a toroidal pore (Yang et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations that agrees with cited experimental findings.

claim: Magainin 2 WT∗ (fully helical) peptides were associated via N- and C-termini.
source: In contrast, Magainin 2 WT∗ (fully helical) peptides were associated via N- and C-termini (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: In Magainin 2 WT∗ synergistic pores, one peptide was largely in a parallel orientation with the membrane plane while the other was inserted in the pore.
source: One peptide was largely in a parallel orientation with the membrane plane while the other was inserted in the pore.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: The angle between the pair of Magainin 2 WT∗ peptides was ∼135°.
source: The angle between the pair of peptides was ∼135°.
evidence: This is a measurement from MARTINI simulations.

claim: δ-lysin peptides associated via C-termini and the interaction took place in the middle of the membrane.
source: However, δ-lysin peptides associated via C-termini and the interaction took place in the middle of the membrane.
evidence: This is a finding from MARTINI simulations.

claim: The structure formed by δ-lysin resembles the hourglass pore observed with peptides containing the helix-kink-helix motif.
source: Such structure resembles the hourglass pore observed with peptides containing the helix-kink-helix motif.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural similarity observed in simulations.

claim: For Buforin II peptides, the largest leakage was observed for P11L, followed by P11A variant.
source: For Buforin II peptides, the largest leakage was observed for P11L, followed by a slightly less hydrophobic P11A variant (see Figure 10).
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence leakage experiments.

claim: Significantly lower leakage was found for Buforin II WT with a proline kink, and the lowest leakage was caused by P11G.
source: Significantly lower leakage was found for Buforin II WT with a proline kink, and the lowest leakage was caused by P11G.
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence leakage experiments.

claim: The leakage results for Buforin II are in excellent agreement with the stability of pores in simulations and previous experimental findings.
source: This is in excellent agreement with the stability of pores in our simulations (see Figure 4 and Figure 7) and previous experimental findings (Kobayashi et al., 2000; Park et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental results with simulations and previous studies.

claim: LL-37 WT peptide exhibited greater leakage than the G14L variant.
source: Moreover, LL-37 WT peptide exhibited greater leakage than the G14L variant, also in agreement with the simulations.
evidence: This is a finding from fluorescence leakage experiments.

claim: Together with the simulation data, the results show that the presence of a flexible kink hinders the formation of barrel-stave but promotes toroidal pores.
source: Together with the simulation data, the results show that the presence of a flexible kink hinders the formation of barrel-stave but promotes toroidal pores.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from both simulation and experimental data.

claim: Two independent models (highly-coarse grained phenomenological model and coarse-grained MARTINI model) and fluorescence leakage experiments consistently showed that flexible kink in helical peptides facilitated the formation of toroidal pores but destabilized barrel-stave pores.
source: Two independent models (highly-coarse grained phenomenological model and coarse-grained MARTINI model) and fluorescence leakage experiments consistently showed that flexible kink in helical peptides facilitated the formation of toroidal pores but destabilized barrel-stave pores.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings from multiple approaches.

claim: Fully helical variants (P11A and P11L) of Buforin II stabilized barrel pores, while the wild-type sequence and P11G variant with a central kink did not.
source: In particular, we found that fully helical variants (P11A and P11L) of Buforin II stabilized barrel pores, while the wild-type sequence and P11G variant with a central kink did not.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from simulations.

claim: The exact structure of toroidal pores (Hourglass or U-shaped) was modulated by the position of the kink in the sequence.
source: The exact structure of toroidal pores (Hourglass or U-shaped) was modulated by the position of the kink in the sequence.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from simulations.

claim: A flexible connection between two helices could have the same effect as a kink within the structure of a single peptide.
source: Moreover, we showed that a flexible connection between two helices could have the same effect as a kink within the structure of a single peptide.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from simulation findings.

claim: Toroidal pores can be stabilized by association between surface-aligned and transmembrane peptides that strongly interact via termini, effectively forming a helix-kink-helix motif.
source: In other words, toroidal pores can also be stabilized by association between surface-aligned and transmembrane peptides that strongly interact via termini, effectively forming a helix-kink-helix motif.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from simulation findings.

claim: Most pore-forming peptides could benefit from the inclusion of proline/glycine residue in the middle of the sequence (if the decreased peptide-membrane interaction is accounted for).
source: As a rule of thumb, most pore-forming peptides could benefit from the inclusion of proline/glycine residue in the middle of the sequence (if the decreased peptide-membrane interaction is accounted for [Krauson et al., 2015]).
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the study findings with a caveat supported by citation.

claim: The majority of the peptides were observed to form toroidal pores and only highly hydrophobic or strongly self-associating peptides to form barrel-stave pores.
source: We observed majority of the peptides to form toroidal pores and only highly hydrophobic or strongly self-associating peptides to form barrel-stave pores.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from simulations.

claim: The obtained molecular understanding could be used for the design of more potent antimicrobial peptides or less toxic drug-carrying peptides.
source: The obtained molecular understanding could be used for the design of more potent antimicrobial peptides or less toxic drug-carrying peptides.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential applications of the findings.

claim: Pore formation in a lipid membrane is an energetically unfavorable process.
source: Pore formation in a lipid membrane is an energetically unfavorable process (Kabelka and Vácha, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: The barrier for pore formation can be decreased by peptide adsorption in a concentration-dependent manner.
source: The barrier for pore formation can be decreased by peptide adsorption in a concentration-dependent manner (Huang and Wu, 1991; Lee et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: AMPs bind more strongly into the highly-curved pore lumen compared to the membrane surface, thus providing a driving force for pore opening.
source: Generally, AMPs bind more strongly into the highly-curved pore lumen compared to the membrane surface, thus providing a driving force for pore opening (Kabelka and Vácha, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: After a critical concentration of AMPs is reached, pore formation becomes spontaneous and observable in experiments.
source: After a critical concentration of AMPs is reached, pore formation becomes spontaneous (Kabelka and Vácha, 2015) and observable in experiments.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and general knowledge.

claim: A designed peptide with similar properties (composed of only leucine and serine residues) was experimentally shown to form pores.
source: A designed peptide with similar properties (composed of only leucine and serine residues) was experimentally shown to form pores (Lear et al., 1988).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Rigid peptides are more suitable for the formation of barrel-stave pores.
source: Firstly, rigid peptides are more suitable for the formation of barrel-stave pores.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the Monte Carlo simulations.

claim: The difference in free energy of pore formation between peptides with and without kink originates in an entropic effect because linear peptides fit better into the geometry of barrel-stave pore and the peptide flexibility hinders the necessary tight packing of the peptides.
source: The difference originates in an entropic effect because linear peptides fit better into the geometry of barrel-stave pore and the peptide flexibility hinders the necessary tight packing of the peptides.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the simulation results.

claim: The peptide rigidity is more important than the chemical nature of the kink-forming residue for the stabilization of barrel-stave pores.
source: Together, these simulations suggest that the peptide rigidity is more important than the chemical nature of the kink-forming residue for the stabilization of barrel-stave pores.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the MARTINI simulations.

claim: The observed effects of increased peptide rigidity on pore stability is in agreement with previously reported experiments.
source: The observed effects of increased peptide rigidity on pore stability is in agreement with previously reported experiments (Kobayashi et al., 2000; Xie et al., 2011; Park et al., 2008; Liu et al., 2011; Jacob et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: An enhanced membrane permeabilization by the more helical P11A variant (compared to WT) of Buforin II has already been experimentally demonstrated.
